newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 22.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The rift in ruling party PASOK over the possibility of Greek-Turkish dialogue following the objections of 32 leading MPs indicates the differences in opinions between the prime minister and government and the party.

--Greek troops arriving in Albania for the multinational protection force received an enthusiastic welcome from Albanians. There was less enthusiasm in Athens, however, for the Italian handling of the multinational force.
--The Preveza coast guard's speedboat - stolen by Albanians over the weekend - is back in Greek hands. The incident however has once again caught the Greek authorities napping

--The first adverse reactions to the government's efforts for Greek-Turkish rapprochement has set off alarm bells in the government's ranks. Athens clarified that the proposed expert committees that would pave the way for a dialogue would have only a "procedural and non-binding" character. From Vienna, Prime Minister Costas Simitis reassured the 32 that there was no dialogue over Ankara's claims in the Aegean and that Greece's three conditions remained.

--More than 5,000 Olympiakos basketball team fans have descended upon Rome for tonight's Final Four semi-final against Ljubljiana of Slovenia. Fans without tickets have been promised a seat by organisers.
--Concerned viewers yesterday threw garbage bags at the Antenna television channel's building in a symbolic protest at the "tele-rubbish" littering the ariwaves.

--Traffic police are imposing draconian measures on the expected increased traffic on the roads ahead of the Greek Orthodox Easter holiday this weekend. Ten died and six were seriously injured in one night in the central town of Larissa, while the toll for the last eight Easter holidays is 222 deaths.

--President of the Republic Kostis Stephanopoulos received criticism from Turkish MPs at the Council of Europe yesterday, who attacked him for his comments regarding Ankara's provocative stance on the Aegean. Stephanopoulos insisted that Ankara continued to flout international law.

--Dimitra Liani-Papandreou, the widow of ruling PASOK's late founder and president, yesterday made her first comments on the lawsuit filed by Papandreous children to reclaim possession of their former home. Today will see an Athens court hearing on the countersuit filed by the present occupant of the house against Liani-Papandreou.

--Reports have Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis threatening to resign if the government continues with its plans for Greek-Turkish dialogue. Arsenis, defence minister at the time of the Imia crisis last year, is reported to have sent Prime Minister Costas Simitis a memorandum on his positions.

--Price increases on fresh produce and meat in Greek Easter week have left Development Minister Vasso Papandreou unconcerned and counselling consumers to avoid buying expensive tomatoes "as they're not in season". Fresh vegetables were up by between 25-67 percent in comparison to last year's prices while the lamb, traditional fare for Greeks at Easter, was up to 2,200 per kilo.
--Civil servants resigning in 1997 will receive increases of up to 16 percent on their pensions and 12 percent on lump sum payments, following adjustments to the new wage scale.

--Some 846 schools have not yet broken up for the Easter holiday, in an effort to make up for lessons lost during the eight-week strike by secondary school teachers earlier this year. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
